comment: Baseline count of `tsc --noEmit` (checkJs) errors. The typecheck enforcement test (tests/typecheck.test.js) asserts the current error count is <= this number. This is a RATCHET: it may only ever be lowered, never raised. New code must not introduce typecheck errors above the baseline; reducing the baseline by adding JSDoc annotations is encouraged. NEVER raise this number to make a failing build pass — fix the code or annotate instead.
notes: Ratchet lowered 89 → 87 on 2026-07-13: the live `tsc --noEmit` (checkJs) count dropped to 87 as JSDoc annotations were added on the audit-wave src/lib modules (hook-deny-signal, approval-ledger, gate-order, circuit-breaker, durable-log), resolving two checkJs inference artifacts. The one-way-ratchet gate (tests/typecheck.test.js) demands the baseline follow the improvement down, so it is set to the measured live count 87. The 87 remaining errors are TypeScript checkJs inference artifacts on un-annotated plain JS (object shapes inferred from first use, Date-string arithmetic, block-scoped duplicate-const false positives) — not runtime bugs. Two genuine bugs surfaced by checkJs were fixed when the baseline was first set: a broken require('./security') in cmd-audit.js and an invalid 3rd argument to fs.readFileSync in staged-files.js. The path to lowering this number further is adding JSDoc @typedef/@param/@returns annotations. NEVER raise it.
